lead: The right Buda Castle tour is the one that fits your visit: a guided walk that takes you inside Matthias Church or the Royal Palace, a vampire and myths walk after dark, a ride up the hill with no climbing, or the cave labyrinth under the hill. This page gets you to that tour in under a minute.

To make the choice easy, I compared all 9 on what really decides it: which entries are included, hours, price per hour, how much climbing there is and where you meet (at the foot of the hill or already at the top), checked on each seller's own page. Filter by entries, night tours, budget or easy access below, or scroll straight to the ranking.

items.skip: if you only want the views and stories: the €16 Royal Cake walk at #2 covers the same streets for €38 less.

review: This is the complete version of a Castle Hill visit. You start at the Holy Trinity Statue and go straight into Matthias Church for 45 minutes with your ticket included, then work south past Fisherman's Bastion and the Hadik statue to the Royal Palace, the Castle Hill Funicular, Matthias Fountain and the Savoy Terrace. In 2.5 hours you see the district's two big set pieces and step inside one of them.

At €54, or €21.60 an hour, it costs three to four and a half times the budget walks. The difference is the church ticket and the guide: this is sold as a historian-led walk, and it carries the best rating of the daytime history walks here. If you would pay for Matthias Church anyway, the gap shrinks fast.

Two things to plan for. You meet at the Holy Trinity Statue on top of the hill, so you need to get up there first. And Fisherman's Bastion is a photo stop, not an entry, so the upper towers are on you. #4 is the cheaper church-entry alternative if you can live with a shorter route.

review: This is the palace tour. An hour outside takes you across the Savoy Terrace, Szent György tér and the Hunyadi and Lion courtyards, then you go inside St Stephen's Hall, the one room of the Royal Palace restored to its pre-war state, for a 30-minute guided visit. Headsets are included, which helps in the busy courtyards.

At €26 for 1.5 hours (€17.35 an hour) it is the only tour here that takes you inside a royal interior. What it does not do is the northern half of the hill: no Matthias Church, no Fisherman's Bastion. Pair it with the €16 cake walk at #2 or the night tour at #5 if you want both.

Be early. The operator asks for 15 minutes before the start because ongoing reconstruction in the palace district makes the Savoy Terrace meeting point hard to find, and latecomers cannot be accommodated. Children under 12 and people with mobility impairments are not accepted.

guide.h2: Which Tours Get You Inside Matthias Church, Fisherman's Bastion and the Palace
guide.html:
• Matthias Church: included on #1 (45 minutes with commentary) and #4 (a full hour, skip-the-line). On #6 it is a paid upgrade. Everyone else walks around it.
  • St Stephen's Hall (Royal Palace): only #3, the one fully restored palace interior. That tour skips Matthias Church and Fisherman's Bastion.
  • Fisherman's Bastion upper towers: not included anywhere. All tours except #3 stop on the Bastion for the Parliament view.
  • Hospital in the Rock: an upgrade on #6, and a stop on the Castle Bus loop.
  • The Labyrinth under the hill: not included on any tour here. Compare the underground options in our Budapest cave tours guide.

• One tour, done properly, church included: Historian-Led Buda Castle Walk (€54).
  • Best value, no entries needed: Buda Castle Walk with Royal Cake (€16).
  • Inside the Royal Palace: Castle Walk with St Stephen's Hall (€26, 1.5 h).
  • Matthias Church for less: Matthias Church and Fisherman's Bastion (€39).
  • After dark with stories: Vampires and Myths Night Tour (€18), or True Crime Walk (€17, 16+).
  • German, French, Italian or Spanish guide, walked up from the Chain Bridge: Castle Hill Tour from Zero Km Stone (€39).
  • Tightest budget or wheelchair user: €12 Buda Castle District Walk.
  • No climbing at all: Official Buda Castle Electric Bus (€18).

Want the rest of the city too? Compare the best walking tours in Budapest, or ride up to Fisherman's Bastion on a Segway or e-bike with our Budapest bike tours comparison.

guide.h2: Practical Tips: Getting Up the Hill, Timing and What Costs Extra
guide.html:
• Where you meet: six of the nine tours start on top of Castle Hill (Holy Trinity Square, Hess András tér or the Savoy Terrace). The night tour (#5), the language tour (#6) and the Castle Bus (#9) start at Clark Ádám tér by the Chain Bridge, on the Buda side at the foot of the hill. No tour here starts on the Pest side.
  • Getting up: walk up from Clark Ádám tér, take the Castle Bus, or join #5, which lets you meet the group at the top.
  • Opening times: Matthias Church closes at 5 pm and often closes during the day for weddings; the Royal Palace museums are closed on Mondays. Book church-entry tours (#1, #4) earlier in the day.
  • Arrive early for St Stephen's Hall: reconstruction in the palace district makes the Savoy Terrace meeting point hard to find, and #3 does not wait for latecomers.
  • What costs extra: tips everywhere, Fisherman's Bastion upper towers on every tour, Matthias Church on all but #1 and #4, food and drinks (except the Dobos torta on #2).
  • What to wear: comfortable shoes for cobblestones and stairs, an umbrella in rain (most walks run rain or shine), warm layers for the night tours.

Finish the day on the river: Castle Hill is at its best lit up from the water on one of the best night cruises in Budapest.

faqs.q: Which Buda Castle tour includes Matthias Church entry?
faqs.a: The Historian-Led Buda Castle Walk (#1, €54) and the Matthias Church and Fisherman's Bastion tour (#4, €39) both include the church ticket and a guided visit inside. On the Castle Hill Tour from the Zero Kilometre Stone (#6) it is a paid upgrade.

faqs.q: Do any tours include the Fisherman's Bastion upper towers?
faqs.a: No. Every tour except the St Stephen's Hall walk stops at Fisherman's Bastion for the view, but none includes the upper towers ticket.

faqs.q: Can I see inside the Royal Palace on a tour?
faqs.a: Yes, on the Buda Castle Walk with St Stephen's Hall (#3, €26). It includes a 30-minute guided visit to St Stephen's Hall, the only fully restored palace interior, and headsets.

faqs.q: How long does a Buda Castle tour take?
faqs.a: Most guided walks take 2 to 2.5 hours. The St Stephen's Hall walk is 1.5 hours, and the Castle Hill Tour with upgrades runs up to 3.5 hours.

faqs.q: Where do Buda Castle tours start?
faqs.a: Most start on top of Castle Hill, at Holy Trinity Square, Hess András tér or the Savoy Terrace. The Vampires night tour, the multilingual Castle Hill Tour and the Castle Bus start at Clark Ádám tér by the Chain Bridge, at the foot of the hill.

faqs.q: Is there a Buda Castle tour for people who cannot walk uphill?
faqs.a: The Official Buda Castle Electric Bus (#9, €18) drives you up and around the hill with 5 stops. The €12 Buda Castle District Walk (#7) is listed as wheelchair accessible, though it starts at the top.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest Buda Castle tour?
faqs.a: The Buda Castle District Walk at €12 for 2 hours (#7). The Royal Cake walk (#2) costs €16 and adds a slice of Dobos torta.

methodology: We compared 9 of the most popular Buda Castle tours side by side: historian-led and budget walks, night tours, the St Stephen's Hall walk, a church-first tour and the official electric Castle Bus. Each was compared on entries included (Matthias Church, Fisherman's Bastion upper towers, St Stephen's Hall), hours, price per hour, group size, languages and where you meet. Prices are live from-prices for a normal date.
